'''''Mesetasaurus''''' ({{lit|Meseta de Artigas lizard}}) is a genus of [[aeolosaurin]] [[titanosaurian]] [[sauropod]] dinosaurs known from the [[Guichón Formation]] ([[Late Cretaceous]], potentially [[Coniacian]] to [[Maastrichtian]]) of [[Paysandú Department]], Uruguay. The genus contains a [[Monotypic taxon|single species]], the [[type species]] '''''Mesetasaurus protector''''', known from two well-preserved caudal vertebrae. It is the second titanosaurian taxon known from its unit and the second non-avian dinosaur described from Uruguay, after the [[saltasauroid]] ''[[Udelartitan]]''.<ref name=Mesetasaurus>{{Cite journal|last1=Soto Núñez  |first1=M. |last2=Montenegro |first2=F. |last3=Perea |first3=D. |year=2026 |title=A new Aeolosaurini (Sauropoda, Titanosauria) from the Upper Cretaceous of Uruguay |journal=[[Ameghiniana]] |doi=10.5710/AMGH.19.06.2026.3689 |url=https://www.ameghiniana.org.ar/index.php/ameghiniana/libraryFiles/downloadPublic/170 |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name="Udelartitan">{{Cite journal|last1=Soto |first1=Matías |last2=Carballido |first2=José L. |last3=Langer |first3=Max C. |last4=Silva Junior |first4=Julian C. G. |last5=Montenegro |first5=Felipe |last6=Perea |first6=Daniel |title=Phylogenetic relationships of a new titanosaur (Dinosauria, Sauropoda) from the Upper Cretaceous of Uruguay |year=2024 |journal=[[Cretaceous Research]] |volume=160 |article-number=105894 |doi=10.1016/j.cretres.2024.105894 |bibcode=2024CrRes.16005894S |hdl=11336/237411 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>

== Discovery and naming ==
The ''Mesetasaurus'' [[holotype]] material consists of two [[caudal vertebrae]], probably corresponding to the third and sixth positions; they were found in the 1980s. They are stored in the Vertebrate Fossil Collection of the [[University of the Republic (Uruguay)|Universidad de la República]] in [[Montevideo]], Uruguay, where they are permanently accessioned under the code FC-DPV 3740. Soto Núñez et al. (2026) further distinguish the more anterior (toward the front) vertebra as 3740A and the more posterior (toward the back) one as 3740B.<ref name=Mesetasaurus />

[[File:Mesetasaurus protector.png|thumb|Hypothetical life reconstruction]]
They were [[species description|described]] as belonging to a new genus and species of titanosaurian dinosaur in 2026. The [[Generic name (biology)|generic name]], ''Mesetasaurus'', refers to the locality where the fossils were found, Meseta de Artigas. The [[specific name]], ''protector'', refers to Uruguayan hero [[José Gervasio Artigas]], also known as {{gloss|Protector de los Pueblos Libres}}; a bust of him is present close to the fossil locality.<ref name=Mesetasaurus />

== Classification ==
To determine the relationships of ''Mesetasaurus'', Soto Núñez et al. (2026) entered it into the [[phylogenetic analysis]] of Pérez Moreno et al. (2026).<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Pérez Moreno |first1=A. |last2=Carballido |first2=J. L. |last3=Otero |first3=A. |last4=Salgado |first4=L. |year=2026 |title=Osteological reassessment of ''Muyelensaurus pecheni'' (Dinosauria: Sauropoda): Systematics and its phylogenetic implications for the clade Rinconsauria |journal=Historical Biology: An International Journal of Paleobiology |pages=1–59 |doi=10.1080/08912963.2025.2585363 }}</ref> This analysis placed ''Mesetasaurus'' in the clade [[Aeolosaurini]], which is split into two smaller clades (named {{gloss|Clade A}} and {{gloss|Clade B}} by the authors). ==Palaeoenvironment==
[[File:Uruguaysuchus BW.jpg|thumb|[[Life restoration]] of the contemporary ''[[Uruguaysuchus]]'']]
''Mesetasaurus'' and its contemporary ''Udelartitan'' are known from the Late Cretaceous [[Guichón Formation]] of Uruguay. The exact age of this formation is uncertain. Some authors have historically suggested a Lower Cretaceous ([[Aptian]]–[[Albian]]) age due to similarities with the [[Migues Formation]].<ref>{{Cite book |last1=de Santa Ana |first1=Héctor |url=https://www.colibri.udelar.edu.uy/jspui/bitstream/20.500.12008/20936/6/Cuencas%20Sedimentarias%20de%20Uruguay%20-%20Mesozoico.pdf |title=Cuencas Sedimentarias de Uruguay: Geología, paleontología y recursos naturales |last2=Goso Aguilar |first2=César |last3=Montaño |first3=Jorge |last4=Piñero |first4=Graciela |last5=Muzio |first5=Rossana |last6=Rossello |first6=Eduardo |last7=Perea |first7=Daniel |last8=Ucha |first8=Nelson |date=2004 |publisher=Universidad de la República |editor-last=Veroslavsky |editor-first=Gerardo |edition=2nd |pages=143–171 |language=es |chapter=El Cretácico post-basáltico y el Terciario Inferior de la Cuenca litoral del río Uruguay: geología y paleontología. |editor-last2=Uvilla |editor-first2=Martín |editor-last3=Martínez |editor-first3=Sergio}}</ref> However, the overlying [[Mercedes Formation, Uruguay|Mercedes Formation]] dates to the [[Campanian]]–[[Maastrichtian]] ages of the [[Upper Cretaceous]], so this would introduce a significant gap in time. The discovery of dinosaur eggshells in the formation similar to ''[[Sphaerovum]]'' prompted later researchers to favor a Late Cretaceous age for the Guichón Formation.<ref name="Soto2012">{{Cite journal |last1=Soto |first1=Matías |last2=Perea |first2=Daniel |last3=Cambiaso |first3=Andrea |date=2012-02-01 |title=First sauropod (Dinosauria: Saurischia) remains from the Guichón Formation, Late Cretaceous of Uruguay |journal=[[Journal of South American Earth Sciences]] |volume=33 |issue=1 |pages=68–79 |doi=10.1016/j.jsames.2011.08.003 |bibcode=2012JSAES..33...68S |issn=0895-9811}}</ref> The describers of ''Mesetasaurus'' suggested that the formation could be further dated to the [[Coniacian]] to [[Maastrichtian]] stages, as that is when other aeolosaurins are known to have lived.<ref name=Mesetasaurus />

Other fossils from the Guichón Formation include several specimens of ''[[Uruguaysuchus]]''—a [[crocodyliform]] closely related to ''[[Araripesuchus]]''—as well as the teeth of indeterminate [[iguanodontia]]ns and [[theropods]].<ref name=Uruguaysuchus2011>{{Cite journal |last1=Soto |first1=Matías |last2=Pol |first2=Diego |last3=Perea |first3=Daniel |date=2012-01-12 |title=A new specimen of ''Uruguaysuchus aznarezi'' (Crocodyliformes: Notosuchia) from the middle Cretaceous of Uruguay and its phylogenetic relationships |journal=[[Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society]] |language=en |volume=163 |pages=S173–S198 |doi=10.1111/j.1096-3642.2011.00717.x|hdl=11336/69086 |hdl-access=free }}</ref><ref name="Soto2012" /> The younger [[Asencio Formation]] of Uruguay also contains titanosaur specimens, including the centrum of a caudal vertebra referred to ''[[Aeolosaurus]]'' sp.<ref name="Udelartitan" />
